newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end just off highs, boosted by Btps.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end just off highs, boosted by Btps.

text.p: Italian shares firmed throughout the session on Thursday, turning down a touch just before the close in line with surging Btp futures which saw a bit of late profit-taking after posting new historic highs, traders said.
Sectors particularly well bid were insurances and some banks but telecoms were mixed and some blue chips like Fiat and Gemina saw position-squaring linked to Friday's futures and options expiries.
The all-share Mibtel index closed 1.53 percent higher at 10,323 after a high of 10,364 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended 1.54 percent up at 15,524 after a peak at 15,608.
Traded volume was estimated at a high 1.25 trillion lire. "It was a pretty hectic session and the enthusiasm underlines the growing optimism of the market," one trader said.
Operators were expecting the government's tough 1997 budget law to get through parliament despite centre-right opposition and barring last-minute surprises.
In insurances, SAI rose 6.39 percent to 13,100 lire, La Fondiaria put on 4.49 percent to 5,860 and Generali gained 3.34 percent to 31,600 lire.
Olivetti, the most traded share, ended 5.72 percent higher at 537.8 lire after a session high of 543.

Telecoms were mixed. Shares in mobile phone operator TIM slipped 0.43 percent to 3,477 lire after Posts Minister Antonio Maccanico said he did not rule out that TIM could be included in the planned Stet-Telecom Italia merger.
Telecoms holding company Stet, however, gained 3.05 percent to 6,174 lire and Telecom Italia put on 2.66 percent to 3,473.

Energy giant ENI gained 1.58 percent to 7,638 lire and Fiat's Snia Fibre unit rose 6.16 percent to 500 lire, but Pirelli lost 0.43 percent to 2,780 and media group Mediaset closed 0.14 percent off at 7,373.
